findings.description: The user_data startup script embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key in plaintext. These credentials are stored in cleartext in the instance metadata, CloudFormation/user-data logs, and the Terraform state, and will be exposed to any user with read access to the instance or logs.
The ingress rule allows SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the host's SSH service to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and unauthorized access attempts.
The EBS volume is created without encryption enabled (the 'encrypted' argument is omitted and left commented out), so data at rest is stored unencrypted on the underlying disks.
The EBS snapshot is created without encryption, propagating the unencrypted data from the unencrypted source volume. Encrypted snapshots should be used for any data containing sensitive information.

map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, meaning instances in this subnet receive a public IP address, expanding the attack surface by making the host directly reachable from the internet (combined with unrestricted SSH/HTTP ingress).
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, meaning instances deployed into this subnet are assigned public IP addresses and become directly reachable from the internet.
